diagnosis: The router accepts workspace_id and user_id but triggers a password reset workflow using user_manager.forgot_password without validating that target_user actually belongs to workspace_id or that current_user has workspace administrator privileges. Any logged-in user can trigger unprompted password reset sequences for arbitrary users across the platform.

corrected_code:
org_users_router = APIRouter(prefix="/workspaces/{workspace_id}/users", tags=["workspace-users"])

@org_users_router.post("/{user_id}/trigger-reset")
async def trigger_workspace_user_reset(
    workspace_id: uuid.UUID,
    user_id: uuid.UUID,
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_session),
    user_manager: BaseUserManager = Depends(get_user_manager),
    current_user: User = Depends(current_active_user)
):
    admin_membership = await db.scalar(
        select(WorkspaceMember).where(
            WorkspaceMember.workspace_id == workspace_id,
            WorkspaceMember.user_id == current_user.id,
            WorkspaceMember.role.in_(["OWNER", "ADMIN"])
        )
    )
    if not admin_membership and not current_user.is_superuser:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Insufficient workspace permissions")

    target_user = await user_manager.get(user_id)
    if not target_user or target_user.workspace_id != workspace_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Target user not found in this workspace")
    
    reset_token = await user_manager.forgot_password(target_user, request)
    return {"status": "reset_dispatched", "user_id": str(user_id)}
